resources.string: Re-encodes videos in this range from H.264 to HEVC, usually about half the size. Slow motion, hyperlapse and other special camera modes are left alone. Uses the delete and \"only keep if smaller\" options above.

Each H.264 video in this range is re-encoded as HEVC on the phone's own encoder. The capture date, location and orientation are copied across and the result is checked against the original before it is kept.

While both exist, the new copy is called name_HEVC.mp4. Once you confirm deleting the original it takes the original's name.

Videos take far longer than photos, and the phone gets warm: best done while charging.

resources.string: Fixes HEICs that show sideways in some viewers (Phone Link, for one) or that have lost their date and sit at the top of the gallery. Checks your whole library, not just this range. Only the photo\'s details are rewritten — never the picture.

This checks every HEIC on the phone and fixes two things:

• Rotation — so photos stand the right way up in every viewer, not just some.
• Capture date — so photos that lost theirs go back where they belong in the gallery. Where the original timezone is unknown, New Zealand time is assumed.

The picture itself is never touched. Android will ask you to allow the changes for photos this app no longer owns.
